activity.note: Sport teacher — on her feet and walking all day. Beach volleyball and cycling on top. Trains 7 days a week: 2 interval runs, 2 zone 2 runs, 1 hybrid, 2–3 strength.

habits.name: Sleep 8h
habits.desc: With 7 sessions a week and a physical job, sleep is the limiting factor.

habits.name: Protein 1.6–2 g/kg
habits.desc: Spread across the day, not all at dinner.

habits.name: Eat enough
habits.desc: Teaching all day plus training: under-eating is the real risk, not over-eating.

habits.name: Forearm and wrist mobility
habits.desc: Your race is decided by grip. Look after it daily.

habits.name: Mobility 10 min
habits.desc: Shoulders and thoracic spine, for the overhead work.

plan.label: Race-specific block — grip and unbroken

days.main: STRENGTH-ENDURANCE 1 · Goblet squat 5×25 @12kg (race weight, unbroken) · DB push press 5×20 @2×6kg · KB deadlift 4×20 @24kg · Ring row 4×12 · Dead bug 3×12
days.sub:
Your two weak stations lead the session. The point is not load — it is finishing 25 reps without putting the weight down.

METRONOME PROTOCOL (you know this from Goliaz): today run it as a plain stopwatch, no beep. The app turns your time into a pace. From Thursday on, the metronome plays at that pace +2 points and you match one rep per beep. Pace = reps/min × 5, so pace 110 is 22 reps/min.
days.pre: Warm-up: 10 min easy bike + shoulder and hip mobility

days.main: INTERVALS 1 · 8×400m at 4:50–5:00/km with 90s walk recovery. After runs 2, 4, 6 and 8, immediately do 20 goblet squats @12kg.
days.sub: This is the race in miniature: arriving at a station with your heart rate already high. Note how the squats feel on the last one.

days.main: ZONE 2 RUN · 50 min continuous at 6:00/km. Nasal breathing for the first 20 min.
days.sub: Genuinely easy. This builds the engine for December, it is not a session to push.

days.main: HYBRID · 4 rounds → 400m run + Farmer carry 60m @2×16kg + 15 DB snatch @9kg per side + 400m run + 20 push press @2×6kg. Rest 2 min between rounds.
days.sub: Full grip circuit. If your hands give out before your legs, that is the finding — tell me and we adjust.

days.main: INTERVALS 2 · 6×600m at 5:00/km with 2 min recovery. Between each: 10 burpee broad jumps.
days.sub: Longer intervals to hold the pace when tired.

days.main: STRENGTH-ENDURANCE 2 + GRIP · Front carry 4×60m @20kg plate · Overhead carry 4×45m @10kg plate · KB clean & press 4×15 · Bear crawl 4×30m · Farmer hold 3×45s @2×20kg
days.sub:
Pure carry day. In this race carries decide more than legs: 240m + 240m + 180m adds up.

Use «Grip circuit» from the templates. No metronome on the carries — just the stopwatch.
days.pre: Warm-up: wrist and forearm mobility, 2 min hang from the bar

days.main: EASY ZONE 2 · 35 min at 6:00/km, or bike 45 min if the legs feel heavy. Mobility 15 min afterwards.

plan.nutr: You already track calories, so the useful part is this: with your job plus 7 sessions a week, the real risk is eating too little, not too much. Protein 1.6–2 g/kg spread across the day. Carbs before and after the two interval days — that is where you need them.

plan.label: Full simulation and sharpening

days.main: STRENGTH-ENDURANCE 1 · Goblet squat 4×30 @12kg unbroken · DB push press 4×25 @2×6kg · KB deadlift 4×20 @24kg · Ring row 3×12
days.sub:
Up from 25 to 30 reps. If 30 unbroken is not there yet, do 25 + 5 after a 10-second pause — and note it.

IMPORTANT: the cadence you can hold for 25 reps is NOT the one you can hold for 60. For the race, aim for about 10–15% below your 25-rep pace. If your best is pace 120 (24 reps/min), plan the race at 100–105 (20–21 reps/min) and you will finish unbroken.

days.main: FULL SIMULATION · The whole race at 85%: 12×400m run with one station between each, in order and at race weights. Time each station and each 400m.
days.sub: The most valuable session of the block. Do not race it — collect data: where you lose time, which station breaks you, how your grip holds. Bring the numbers to me.
days.pre: Race-day protocol: same breakfast, same kit, same shoes as you will use in London

days.main: RECOVERY · 30 min very easy, or a walk if you feel yesterday in your legs.
INTERVALS 1 · 10×400m at 4:50/km with 90s walk. No stations today — pure speed.
days.sub: Faster than race pace so that race pace feels comfortable.

days.main: WEAK STATIONS · Goblet squat 3×30 @12kg · DB push press 3×25 @2×6kg · Devil press 3×10 @2×5kg · Overhead carry 3×45m
days.sub: Short session, only what you need. Use «Both weak stations — race rhythm» from the templates, at your race cadence — not your maximum. Today you are rehearsing the rhythm you will actually use in London.

days.main: ZONE 2 RUN · 45 min at 6:00/km.
MOBILITY 25 min · Shoulders, thoracic spine, hips and forearms. Plus a 20 min walk.
days.sub: Last easy Sunday before race week.

plan.nutr: Simulation day: eat exactly what you plan to eat in London. Breakfast 2–3 h before, mostly carbs. If the race takes you over an hour, practise drinking during it too. Nothing new after this week.

plan.label: Taper — Deadly Dozen World Championship

days.main: ACTIVATION · Goblet squat 3×15 @12kg · Push press 3×15 @2×6kg · Farmer carry 2×40m. Everything at 60%, well short of failure.
days.sub: Keeping the pattern alive without generating fatigue. Run the template at your race cadence minus 2 points: it should feel easy.

days.main: SHARPENING · 5×400m at race pace (4:50–5:00/km) with full recovery between. Between runs 2 and 4: 10 goblet squats.
days.sub: Short and sharp. Legs awake, no fatigue.

days.main: EASY · 30 min at 6:00/km with 4×20s strides at the end.
TECHNICAL RUN-THROUGH · One round at 50%: 400m + 15 goblet squats + 15 push press + 40m farmer carry + 10 snatch. 20 min total.
days.sub: Rehearse transitions: picking the weight up, putting it down, moving off. Seconds live there.

days.main: FULL REST · Travel to London. 3L water. Carbs at every meal. Sleep 8h+.
days.sub: Day −1: nothing new, no long walks around the city. Prepare kit and numbers tonight.

days.main: DEADLY DOZEN WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP — London
days.sub: Strategy: the first two 400s will feel too easy — that is correct, do not chase anyone. Grip is your budget for the whole race: on farmer and front carry, walk fast with a firm grip rather than gripping desperately. On goblet squats and push press, set a rhythm from rep 1 that you know you can hold for 60, and never break it. Chalk before every carry.

days.main: Second race day if you compete again, or active recovery: 20 min walk, 20 min mobility, high protein.

plan.nutr: Race week: carbs up slightly from Thursday, nothing new from Friday. Breakfast 2–3 h before your start, mostly carbs and low fibre. Caffeine only if you already use it in training. Afterwards: 30–40 g protein plus carbs within the hour.

plan.label: Recovery and transition to HYROX

days.main: Complete rest. Write down everything you remember from the race while it is fresh: station times, where you broke, how your grip held.
days.sub: Those notes are what we will build the HYROX block on.

days.main: EASY · 30 min at 6:00/km. Just moving.
MOBILITY 25 min · Shoulders and forearms above all — they took the most load.
LIGHT FULL BODY · Goblet squat 3×15 · Ring row 3×12 · Push press 3×12 · Dead bug 3×12. Comfortable weights.
days.sub: Back to moving without pushing.

days.main: ZONE 2 RUN · 45 min at 6:00/km.
days.sub: From here the HYROX block starts: more continuous aerobic volume, less pure grip work.

days.main: FIRST HYROX CONTACT · 4 rounds → 500m row + 15 wall balls + 400m run. Easy pace, learning the pattern.
days.sub: HYROX in December is a different animal: 8 km of running and a sled. We will start building that from next week.

days.main: Rest. Tell Miguel how the race went and we will build the December block.

plan.nutr: Recovery week: keep protein high, do not cut calories. This is when the adaptation from the last three weeks actually lands.

presets.name: Goblet squat — unbroken builder
presets.note: Session 1: no metronome, plain stopwatch — that sets your baseline pace. From then on the metronome runs at your previous pace +2 and you match every rep to the beep.

presets.name: Push press — unbroken builder
presets.note: Same protocol. Push press punishes a broken rhythm more than squats: if you speed up early you will stall around rep 40.

presets.name: Both weak stations — race rhythm
presets.note: The pair back to back, as they come in the race. Hold the cadence even when it feels slow at the start.

presets.name: Grip circuit
presets.note: No metronome on the carries — the stopwatch is enough. On the deadlifts, keep the beep: that is where rhythm saves you time.
